task.title: Materialize a bounded due recurrence page atomically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/925 by atomically binding one bounded inclusive-cutoff due page to an ordered vector of caller-owned task identities.
acceptance_criteria: Select one exact recurrence page in authored order and require exactly one distinct caller-supplied task identity per selected coordinate.
Recheck recurrence revision, occurrence stream absence, and task stream absence in one immediate transaction and return ordered bindings plus next_offset.
Commit the complete page or none on count mismatch, duplicate identity, collision, stale definition, corruption, serialization, storage, or racing-writer failure.

attempts.summary: Established RED behavior and concurrency coverage.
attempts.diagnostic: Kernel integration tests failed because materialize_due_occurrences_page and its typed task identity shape errors did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added tests for ordered success, empty future pages, finite and cutoff truncation, count and duplicate rejection, collisions, corruption, rollback, and races before production behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Added an event-log batch primitive and materialize_due_occurrences_page, reusing bounded due-page projection and exact replay to commit every occurrence-task binding together.
attempts.patch: Implemented the kernel transaction in scheduler.rs and event_log.rs and documented caller-owned cutoff and identity-vector authority in ADR-0066.

attempts.summary: Completed substantive exact-head review and bounded refactor disposition.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit's genuine review raised three trivial non-blocking suggestions: wider encode_event reuse, zip-based slice construction, and replacing an unreachable fallback with a typed event-log error. The third was categorized as stability and availability because the no-conflict assumption depends on storage invariants and internal check ordering, so a typed fallback would remove a possible library panic. The one-commit exact head passed the Rust gate and no review thread was reported; all three suggestions were deferred rather than misreported as fixed.
attempts.patch: Kept the new batch primitive crate-private, reused due-page and materialized-page projections, and avoided unrelated refactoring while preserving the review lessons.

outcome.summary: The kernel materializes one caller-selected due page without partial occurrence provenance, orphan tasks, generated identity, ambient clock policy, or execution grants.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0192-atomic-due-recurrence-materialization.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 193 records: 193 valid, 0 invalid
Pull request 926 exact head 7ed51199351cfad90bfeeb5ecdfd55f614fd166b squash merge 7faafff0ca4c2742c73bdc0dcc8d2dda12538d57

lessons: A page of occurrence-task bindings is one crash-consistency unit and must not be implemented as repeated single-coordinate transactions.
Task count and order prove that the caller owns identity allocation and binding policy rather than the kernel.
Future empty pages require zero identities and must perform no writes.
Substantive review nitpicks should be preserved accurately without claiming they were fixed or treating them as blockers.
Materialization grants no claim, lease, dispatch, retry, permission, workflow, provider, tool, or execution authority.
